```{r}
finalidk$tract_white_perc=as.numeric(finalidk$tract_white_perc)
finalidk$Rooms=as.numeric(finalidk$Rooms)

finalidk$Bedrooms=as.numeric(finalidk$Bedrooms)
finalidk$Near.Major.Road = as.character(finalidk$Near.Major.Road)
finalidk$Wall.Material = as.character(finalidk$Wall.Material)
finalidk$Roof.Material = as.character(finalidk$Roof.Material)
finalidk$Garage.indicator = as.character(finalidk$Garage.indicator)
finalidk$Porch = as.character(finalidk$Porch)
finalidk$Garage.indicator = as.character(finalidk$Garage.indicator)
finalidk$Construction.Quality = as.character(finalidk$Construction.Quality)
finalidk$Use = as.character(finalidk$Use)
finalidk$Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.=as.numeric(finalidk$Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.)
finalidk$Land.Square.Feet=as.numeric(finalidk$Land.Square.Feet)



finalidk$binary_max <- ifelse(finalidk$Max < 10, 0, 1)
finalidk$class_max <- cut(finalidk$Max, 
                           breaks = c(0, 5, 10, 15, Inf), 
                           labels = c("0ppb-5ppb", "5ppb-10ppb", "10ppb-15ppb", "15ppb+"), 
                           right = FALSE)  # Excludes upper bound in each range
finalidk$class <- cut(finalidk$Max, 
                           breaks = c(0, 5, 10, Inf), 
                           labels = c("0ppb-5ppb", "5ppb-10ppb", "10ppb+"), 
                           right = FALSE)  # Excludes upper bound in each range
```

```{r}
variables <- c("Age",  "Bedrooms",  "tract_white_perc", "Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.", "Land.Square.Feet", "Near.Major.Road")

all_models_logit <- list()
aic_values <- numeric()

for (i in 1:length(variables)) {
  subsets <- combn(variables, i, simplify = FALSE)
  for (subset in subsets) {
    formula_str <- paste("finalidk$binary_max ~", paste(paste0("finalidk$`", subset, "`"), collapse = " + "))
    model <- glm(as.formula(formula_str), family=binomial(link = "logit"))
    all_models_logit[[formula_str]] <- summary(model)
    aic_values[formula_str] <- AIC(model)
  }
}


# Sort the AIC values to get the models with the lowest AIC
sorted_aic_values <- sort(aic_values)

# Get the top 25 models with the lowest AICs
top_25_models <- all_models_logit[names(sorted_aic_values[1:25])]

# Print the top 25 AICs with their formulas
```

lowest aic--i built it into my models above no need for it

```{r}
# Create an empty list to store models
all_models_logit <- list()
# Create an empty vector to store AIC values for each model
aic_values <- c()

# Loop over the number of predictors in subsets
for (i in 1:length(variables)) {
    subsets <- combn(variables, i, simplify = FALSE)
    
    # Loop over each subset of predictors
    for (subset in subsets) {
        # Create the formula as a string
        formula_str <- paste("binary_max ~", paste(subset, collapse = " + "))
        
        # Fit the logistic regression model
        model <- glm(as.formula(formula_str), data = finalidk, family = binomial(link = "logit"))
        
        # Store the model in the list
        all_models_logit[[formula_str]] <- model
        
        # Extract AIC and add it to the AIC values vector
        aic_values[formula_str] <- AIC(model)
    }
}

# Sort the AIC values to get the models with the lowest AIC
sorted_aic_values <- sort(aic_values)

# Get the top 25 models with the lowest AICs
top_25_models <- all_models_logit[names(sorted_aic_values[1:25])]

# Print the top 25 AICs with their formulas
top_25_models
```

PCA regression--good

```{r}
library(pls)
library(caret)
variables <- c("Age", "tract_pop", "Rooms", "Bedrooms",  "tract_white_perc", "Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.", "Land.Square.Feet")
# Select only relevant columns
data_pcr <- finalidk[, c("Max", variables)]  

# Remove rows with NA values
data_pcr <- na.omit(data_pcr)

# Standardize predictors (important for PCA)
predictors <- scale(data_pcr[, variables])
response <- data_pcr$Max

# Fit PCR model using cross-validation
pcr_model <- pcr(response ~ predictors, data = data_pcr, scale = TRUE, validation = "CV")

# Summary of PCR model
summary(pcr_model)

validationplot(pcr_model, val.type = "MSEP")  # Mean Squared Error Plot
coef(pcr_model, ncomp = 6)  # Example: Using 2 principal components
predictions <- predict(pcr_model, ncomp = 3, newdata = data_pcr)

# Compute R-squared and RMSE
actuals <- response
rss <- sum((actuals - predictions)^2)
tss <- sum((actuals - mean(actuals))^2)
r_squared <- 1 - (rss/tss)
rmse <- sqrt(mean((actuals - predictions)^2))

cat("R-squared:", r_squared, "\nRMSE:", rmse, "\n")

```

```{r}
train_indices <- sample(1:nrow(finalidk_clean), size = 0.6 * nrow(finalidk_clean))

# Ensure data is in data frame format

# Fit a Bagging model

                        Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. , 
                        data = train_df, nbagg = 100)

# Print model summary
summary(bagging_model)
# Predict probabilities
bagging_prob <- predict(bagging_model, newdata = test_data, type = "prob")

# Convert probabilities to class labels (threshold = 0.5)
bagging_predictions <- ifelse(bagging_prob > 0.5, 1, 0)

# Ensure predictions and test response are factors
bagging_predictions <- as.factor(bagging_predictions)
test_response <- as.factor(test_response)

# Create Confusion Matrix
conf_matrix <- table(Actual = test_response, Predicted = bagging_predictions)
print(conf_matrix)
```

```{r}
# Remove unnecessary columns

test_data <- finalidk_clean[-train_indices, ]

# Fit Decision Tree (classification)

                    tract_white_perc + Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. + 
                    Land.Square.Feet , 
                    data = train_data, method = "class")

# Make Predictions on the Test Set
```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(ggplot2)

# Assuming finalidk_clean is your cleaned dataset

# Select the features you want to use for clustering
features <- finalidk_clean[, c("Age", "Rooms", "Bedrooms", 
                                 "tract_white_perc", 
                                 "Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.", 
                                 "Land.Square.Feet")]

# Scale the features
features_scaled <- scale(features)

# Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

# Determine the number of clusters (k)
k <- 5  # You can experiment with different values of k

# Run K-means clustering
kmeans_result <- kmeans(features_scaled, centers = k, nstart = 25)

# Print the clustering results
print(kmeans_result)

# Add cluster assignments to the original dataset
finalidk_clean$Cluster <- as.factor(kmeans_result$cluster)

# Visualize the clusters (using first two features for 2D visualization)
ggplot(finalidk_clean, aes(x = Age, y = Rooms, color = Cluster)) +
  geom_point() +
  labs(title = "K-means Clustering", x = "Age", y = "Max") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
  predictions[[as.character(cluster)]] <- model3
  model_summaries[[as.character(cluster)]] <- summary(model3)  # Store the summary for each cluster
  cluster_data$Predicted_Max <- predict(model3, newdata = cluster_data, type = "response")
  
  finalidk_clean[finalidk_clean$Cluster == cluster, "Predicted_Max"] <- cluster_data$Predicted_Max
}

# Now you can inspect summaries for each model
model_summaries
```

```{r}
# Elbow Method to determine optimal k
wss <- numeric(10)  # Vector to store within-cluster sum of squares
for (i in 1:10) {
  kmeans_model <- kmeans(features_scaled, centers = i, nstart = 25)
  wss[i] <- kmeans_model$tot.withinss
}

# Plot the Elbow Method
plot(1:10, wss, type = "b", pch = 19, xlab = "Number of Clusters (k)", 
     ylab = "Total Within-Cluster Sum of Squares", 
     main = "Elbow Method for K-means Clustering")
```

```{r}
variables <- c("Age",   "Bedrooms",  "tract_white_perc", "Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.", "Land.Square.Feet", "Near.Major.Road")

all_models_logit3 <- list()
aic_values4 <- numeric()

for (i in 1:length(variables)) {
  subsets <- combn(variables, i, simplify = FALSE)
  for (subset in subsets) {
    formula_str <- paste("schoollevel_data$binary_max ~", paste(paste0("schoollevel_data$`", subset, "`"), collapse = " + "))
    model <- glm(as.formula(formula_str), family=binomial(link = "logit"))
    all_models_logit3[[formula_str]] <- summary(model)
    aic_values4[formula_str] <- AIC(model)
  }
}


# Sort the AIC values to get the models with the lowest AIC
sorted_aic_values4 <- sort(aic_values4)

# Get the top 25 models with the lowest AICs
top_25_models4 <- all_models_logit3[names(sorted_aic_values4[1:25])]

# Print the top 25 AICs with their formulas
```

```{r}

variables <- c("Age",  "Bedrooms",  "tract_white_perc", "Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.", "Land.Square.Feet", "Near.Major.Road")

all_models_logit9 <- list()
aic_values9 <- numeric()

for (i in 1:2) {
  subsets <- combn(variables, i, simplify = FALSE)
  for (subset in subsets) {
    formula_str <- paste("wardlevel_data$binary_max ~", paste(paste0("wardlevel_data$`", subset, "`"), collapse = " * "))
    model <- glm(as.formula(formula_str), family=binomial(link = "logit"))
    all_models_logit9[[formula_str]] <- summary(model)
    aic_values9[formula_str] <- AIC(model)
  }
}


# Sort the AIC values to get the models with the lowest AIC
sorted_aic_values9 <- sort(aic_values9)

# Get the top 25 models with the lowest AICs
top_25_models9 <- all_models_logit9[names(sorted_aic_values9[1:25])]

# Print the top 25 AICs with their formulas
```

```{r}
library(MASS)
variables <- c("Age",  "Bedrooms",  "tract_white_perc", "ward" )

all_models_logit81 <- list()
aic_values81 <- numeric()

for (i in 1:length(variables)) {
  subsets <- combn(variables, i, simplify = FALSE)
  for (subset in subsets) {
    formula_str <- paste("finalidk$class_max ~", paste("finalidk$`Age` * finalidk$`ward` +", 
                  paste0("finalidk$`", subset, "`"), collapse = " + "))
    model <- polr(as.formula(formula_str), method = "logistic")
    all_models_logit81[[formula_str]] <- summary(model)
    aic_values81[formula_str] <- AIC(model)
  }
}


# Sort the AIC values to get the models with the lowest AIC
sorted_aic_values81 <- sort(aic_values81)

# Get the top 25 models with the lowest AICs
top_25_models81 <- all_models_logit81[names(sorted_aic_values81[1:25])]

# Print the top 25 AICs with their formulas
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)

# Create a data frame with coefficients and confidence intervals
coef_data <- data.frame(
  coeff_names = c(
    "Bedrooms", "White Perct", "Population", "Wall Material: 2", "Wall Material: 3", "Wall Material: 4",
    "Roof Material: 2", "Roof Material: 3", "Roof Material: 4", "Roof Material: 5", "Roof Material: 6",
     "Age", "Near Major Road"
  ),
  estimates = c(
    -4.794e-02, 1.597e-01, -1.644e-05, 8.279e-02, 5.199e-02, 2.323e-01, 
    -2.695e-01, -1.634e-01, 3.200e-02, 6.711e-02, -1.363e-01, 
     1.854e-03, 
    -3.238e-01
  ),
  std_errors = c(
    9.254e-03, 9.758e-03, NA, 2.296e-02, 1.961e-02, 8.479e-04, 
    9.576e-03, 9.383e-05, 2.268e-05, 1.348e-04, 4.030e-04, 
    
    1.184e-03, 1.266e-03
  )
)



# Calculate confidence intervals
coef_data$Lower <- coef_data$estimates - 1.96 * coef_data$std_errors
coef_data$Upper <- coef_data$estimates + 1.96 * coef_data$std_errors

# Plot using ggplot2
ggplot(coef_data, aes(x = estimates, y = reorder(coeff_names, estimates))) +
  geom_point(color = "blue", size = 3) +  # Point estimates
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = Lower, xmax = Upper), height = 0.2, color = "black") +  # CI bars
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Forest Plot of Model Coefficients",
       x = "Coefficient Estimate",
       y = "Predictor Variable") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "red")  # Reference line at 0
```

```{r}

ordinal_model <- polr(finalidk$class_max ~   finalidk$`tract_white_perc` + finalidk$tract_pop + finalidk$Wall.Material+finalidk$Roof.Material+  finalidk$`Bedrooms` + finalidk$`Near.Major.Road`+ finalidk$Land.Square.Feet +finalidk$Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.+ finalidk$Age *finalidk$ward , method="logistic"
                    )
library(broom)
library(dplyr)

coef_df=coef(ordinal_model)
coef_df=as.data.frame(coef_df)
coef_df$predictor <- rownames(coef_df)  # Convert row names to a column
colnames(coef_df) <- c("estimate", "predictor")  # Rename columns


# Check the result
head(coef_df)

# Subset the data to rows 2 through 11 and rows 61 through 63
coef_data_subset <- coef_df %>%
  slice(1:15)


ggplot(coef_data_subset, aes(x = reorder(predictor, estimate), y = estimate, fill = estimate > 0)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", show.legend = FALSE) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("red", "green")) +  # Red for negative, green for positive
  theme_minimal() +
  coord_flip() +  # Flip the axes for easier reading of labels
  labs(title = "Coefficient Plot: Positive vs Negative Effects",
       x = "Predictor Variable",
       y = "Coefficient Estimate")

```

```{r}
)
```

```{r}
# Compute the linear predictor (z)
z <- sum(unlist(coefficients) * unlist(variables))

# Compute cumulative probabilities using the logistic CDF
p_0_5 <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(intercepts[1] - z)))
p_5_10 <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(intercepts[2] - z))) - p_0_5
p_10_15 <- 1 / (1 + exp(-(intercepts[3] - z))) - (p_0_5 + p_5_10)
p_15_plus <- 1 - (p_0_5 + p_5_10 + p_10_15)

# Output the probabilities
probabilities <- list(
  "0-5 ppb" = p_0_5,
  "5-10 ppb" = p_5_10,
  "10-15 ppb" = p_10_15,
  "15+ ppb" = p_15_plus
)

print(probabilities)
```

```{r}
# Load necessary library
library(MASS)

# Fit the ordinal regression model
ordinal_model <- polr(finalidk$class_max ~   finalidk$`tract_white_perc` + finalidk$tract_pop + finalidk$Wall.Material+finalidk$Roof.Material+  finalidk$`Bedrooms` + finalidk$`Near.Major.Road`+ finalidk$Land.Square.Feet +finalidk$Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.+ finalidk$Age *finalidk$ward , method="logistic"
                    )

# Define the specific house's predictor values
specific_house <- data.frame(
  Bedrooms = 2,
  tract_white_perc = 0.75,
  Age = 120,
  tract_pop= 6000,
  ward11=1,
  Near.Major.Road1 = 1,
  Land.Square.Feet=5000,
  Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.=80000,
  Roof.Material4=1,
  Wall.Material2=1

  
  
  
)

# Compute linear predictor (z) for the specific house
z_specific <- sum(coef(ordinal_model) * as.numeric(specific_house))

# Compute odds of being above 5 ppb (e.g., in 5-10 ppb or higher)
intercept_1 <- ordinal_model$zeta[2]  # First threshold (0-5 ppb)
odds_above_5 <- exp(z_specific - intercept_1)

# Print the odds
print(odds_above_5)
```

```{r}
# Given house characteristics
Bedrooms <- 2

Age <- 120
tract_pop <- 6000
ward11 <- 1
Near.Major.Road1 <- 1
Land.Square.Feet <- 5000
Prior.Tax.Value <- 80000
Roof.Material4 <- 1
Wall.Material2 <- 1

# Coefficients from the model
coefs <- c(
  tract_white_perc = 2.763471e-01, 
  tract_pop = -1.753025e-05, 
  Wall.Material2 = 8.158228e-02, 
  Roof.Material4 = 3.402460e-02, 
  Bedrooms = -4.622626e-02, 
  Near.Major.Road1 = -3.209896e-01, 
  Land.Square.Feet = 4.248468e-05, 
  Prior.Tax.Value = -2.398436e-06, 
  Age = 1.953531e-03, 
  ward11 = 2.876365e-01, 
  `Age:ward11` = 5.570581e-03
)

# Compute the log-odds
log_odds <- tract_white_perc * coefs["tract_white_perc"] +
            tract_pop * coefs["tract_pop"] +
            Wall.Material2 * coefs["Wall.Material2"] +
            Roof.Material4 * coefs["Roof.Material4"] +
            Bedrooms * coefs["Bedrooms"] +
            Near.Major.Road1 * coefs["Near.Major.Road1"] +
            Land.Square.Feet * coefs["Land.Square.Feet"] +
            Prior.Tax.Value * coefs["Prior.Tax.Value"] +
            Age * coefs["Age"] +
            ward11 * coefs["ward11"] +
            Age * ward11 * coefs["Age:ward11"]

# Convert to odds ratio
odds_ratio <- exp(log_odds)

# Print results
cat("Log-Odds:", log_odds, "\n")
cat("Odds Ratio:", odds_ratio, "\n")
```

```{r}
bootstrap_stratified <- function(data, indices) {
  sampled_data <- data %>%
    group_by(ward) %>%
    sample_n(size = min(table(data$ward)), replace = TRUE) %>%  # Balance wards
    ungroup()
  
   return(quantile(sampled_data$Max, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE))  # 90th percentile
}
```

```{r}
bootstrap_stratified <- function(data, indices) {
  sampled_data <- data %>%
    group_by(ward) %>%
    sample_n(size = min(table(data$ward)), replace = TRUE) %>%  # Balance wards
    ungroup()
  
  # Count the number of draws in each class (assuming 'classnin' is the class variable)
  class_counts <- table(sampled_data$class_max)
  
  return(class_counts)
}

set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility
boot_results <- boot(data = finalidk, statistic = bootstrap_stratified, R = 200)

# View results
print(boot_results)
```

```{r}
library(MASS)
# Initialize an empty list to store models for each neighborhood
neighborhood_models <- list()

# Iterate over each unique neighborhood
for (neighborhood in unique(merged_data$sec_neigh)) {
  # Subset the data for the current neighborhood
  neighborhood_data <- merged_data %>% 
    filter(sec_neigh == neighborhood) %>%
    drop_na(tract_white_perc, Bedrooms, Land.Square.Feet, 
            Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land., Age)
  
  # Check if there is enough data for model fitting (at least 4 rows)
  if (nrow(neighborhood_data) >= 4) {
    # Convert categorical response variable to ordered factor
    neighborhood_data$class_max <- as.ordered(neighborhood_data$class_max)
    
    # Try fitting the logistic regression model
    model <- tryCatch({
      polr(class_max ~ tract_white_perc + Bedrooms + Land.Square.Feet + 
             Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. + Age, 
           data = neighborhood_data)
    }, error = function(e) {
      # In case of error, print the error message
      print(paste("Error in processing", neighborhood, ":", e$message))
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    # Store the model if it's valid
    if (!is.null(model)) {
      neighborhood_models[[neighborhood]] <- model
    }
  } else {
    print(paste("Not enough data for neighborhood:", neighborhood))
  }
}

# View the list of models (for example, for Norwood Park)
print(neighborhood_models[["Norwood Park"]])
```

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(nnet)
library(dplyr)

# Initialize an empty list to store models for each neighborhood
neighborhood_models <- list()

# Initialize an empty data frame to store coefficients
coefficients_df <- data.frame(
  neighborhood = character(),
  category = character(),
  variable = character(),
  coefficient = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Iterate over each unique neighborhood
for (neighborhood in unique(merged_data$sec_neigh)) {
  
  # Subset the data for the current neighborhood
  neighborhood_data <- merged_data %>% 
    filter(sec_neigh == neighborhood) %>%
    drop_na(tract_white_perc, Bedrooms, Land.Square.Feet, 
            Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land., Age, class_max)
  
  # Check if there is enough data for model fitting (at least 4 rows)
  if (nrow(neighborhood_data) >= 4) {
    
    # Convert response variable to ordered factor
    neighborhood_data$class_max <- as.ordered(neighborhood_data$class_max)
    
    # Fit multinomial logistic regression model
    model <- tryCatch({
      multinom(class_max ~ tract_white_perc + Bedrooms + Land.Square.Feet + 
                 Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. + Age, 
               data = neighborhood_data)
    }, error = function(e) {
      print(paste("Error in processing", neighborhood, ":", e$message))
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    # Store the model if it's valid
    if (!is.null(model)) {
      neighborhood_models[[neighborhood]] <- model
      
      # Extract coefficients and ensure proper structure
      model_coefficients <- coef(model)  
      
      # Check if coefficients are properly structured
      if (!is.null(dim(model_coefficients))) {
        
        # Convert coefficient matrix into long format
        temp_df <- as.data.frame(as.table(model_coefficients))  
        colnames(temp_df) <- c("category", "variable", "coefficient")  # Rename columns
        
        # Add neighborhood information
        temp_df$neighborhood <- neighborhood
        
        # Append to the coefficients dataframe
        coefficients_df <- rbind(coefficients_df, temp_df)
        
      } else {
        print(paste("Warning: No valid coefficients for neighborhood:", neighborhood))
      }
    }
    
  } else {
    print(paste("Not enough data for neighborhood:", neighborhood))
  }
}

# View the resulting coefficients data frame
print(coefficients_df)
```

```{r}
 # Load required packages
library(nnet)
library(dplyr)
library(MASS)  # polr() function for ordered logistic regression

# Initialize an empty list to store models for each neighborhood
neighborhood_models <- list()

# Initialize an empty data frame to store coefficients
coefficients_df <- data.frame(
  neighborhood = character(),
  variable = character(),
  coefficient = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Iterate over each unique neighborhood
for (neighborhood in unique(merged_data$pri_neigh)) {
  
  # Subset the data for the current neighborhood
  neighborhood_data <- merged_data %>% 
    filter(pri_neigh == neighborhood) %>%
    drop_na(tract_white_perc, Bedrooms, Land.Square.Feet, 
            Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land., Age, class_max)
  
  # Check if there is enough data for model fitting (at least 4 rows)
  if (nrow(neighborhood_data) >= 4) {
    
    # Convert response variable to ordered factor
    neighborhood_data$class_max <- as.ordered(neighborhood_data$class_max)
    
    # Fit ordered logistic regression model
    model <- tryCatch({
      polr(class_max ~ tract_white_perc + Bedrooms + Land.Square.Feet + 
             Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. + Age, 
           data = neighborhood_data, method = "logistic")
    }, error = function(e) {
      print(paste("Error in processing", neighborhood, ":", e$message))
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    # Store the model if it's valid
    if (!is.null(model)) {
      neighborhood_models[[neighborhood]] <- model
      
      # Extract coefficients
      model_coefficients <- coef(model)  
      
      # Ensure coefficient names exist
      coef_names <- if (length(model_coefficients) > 0) names(model_coefficients) else character(0)
      
      # Create a temporary data frame only if coefficients exist
      if (length(model_coefficients) > 0) {
        temp_df <- data.frame(
          neighborhood = neighborhood,
          variable = coef_names,
          coefficient = as.vector(model_coefficients),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
        
        # Append to the main coefficients dataframe
        coefficients_df <- rbind(coefficients_df, temp_df)
      }
    }
    
  } else {
    print(paste("Not enough data for neighborhood:", neighborhood))
  }
}

# View the resulting coefficients data frame
print(coefficients_df)
```

```{r}
# Load required packages
library(nnet)
library(dplyr)
library(MASS)  # polr() function for ordered logistic regression

# Initialize an empty list to store models for each neighborhood
neighborhood_models <- list()

# Initialize an empty data frame to store coefficients and intercepts
coefficients_df <- data.frame(
  neighborhood = character(),
  variable = character(),
  coefficient = numeric(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Iterate over each unique neighborhood
for (neighborhood in unique(merged_data$sec_neigh)) {
  
  # Subset the data for the current neighborhood
  neighborhood_data <- merged_data %>% 
    filter(sec_neigh == neighborhood) %>%
    drop_na(tract_white_perc, Bedrooms, Land.Square.Feet, 
            Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land., Age, class_max)
  
  # Check if there is enough data for model fitting (at least 4 rows)
  if (nrow(neighborhood_data) >= 4) {
    
    # Convert response variable to ordered factor
    neighborhood_data$class_max <- as.ordered(neighborhood_data$class_max)
    
    # Fit ordered logistic regression model
    model <- tryCatch({
      polr(class_max ~ tract_white_perc + Bedrooms + Land.Square.Feet + 
             Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. + Age, 
           data = neighborhood_data, method = "logistic")
    }, error = function(e) {
      print(paste("Error in processing", neighborhood, ":", e$message))
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    # Store the model if it's valid
    if (!is.null(model)) {
      neighborhood_models[[neighborhood]] <- model
      
      # Extract coefficients
      model_coefficients <- coef(model)  
      coef_names <- if (length(model_coefficients) > 0) names(model_coefficients) else character(0)
      
      # Extract intercepts (thresholds)
      model_intercepts <- model$zeta  
      intercept_names <- if (length(model_intercepts) > 0) names(model_intercepts) else character(0)
      
      # Create a temporary data frame for coefficients
      if (length(model_coefficients) > 0) {
        temp_coef_df <- data.frame(
          neighborhood = neighborhood,
          variable = coef_names,
          coefficient = as.vector(model_coefficients),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
        coefficients_df <- rbind(coefficients_df, temp_coef_df)
      }
      
      # Create a temporary data frame for intercepts
      if (length(model_intercepts) > 0) {
        temp_intercept_df <- data.frame(
          neighborhood = neighborhood,
          variable = intercept_names,
          coefficient = as.vector(model_intercepts),
          stringsAsFactors = FALSE
        )
        coefficients_df <- rbind(coefficients_df, temp_intercept_df)
      }
    }
    
  } else {
    print(paste("Not enough data for neighborhood:", neighborhood))
  }
}

# View the resulting coefficients and intercepts data frame
print(coefficients_df)
```

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggnewscale)

# Filter the variables
vars <- c("Age", "Bedrooms", "Land.Square.Feet", 
          "Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land.", "tract_white_perc")

df <- coefficients_df %>%
  filter(variable %in% vars)

# Set up base plot
p <- ggplot()

# Loop through each variable, add its own tile layer and fill scale
for (i in seq_along(vars)) {
  v <- vars[i]
  df_var <- df %>% filter(variable == v) %>% mutate(xvar = v)  # Fixed x-position
  
  p <- p +
    geom_tile(data = df_var, aes(x = xvar, y = neighborhood, fill = coefficient)) +
    scale_fill_gradient2(
      low = "lightgreen", mid = "skyblue", high = "purple", midpoint = 0,
      name = v
    )
  
  if (i < length(vars)) {
    p <- p + ggnewscale::new_scale_fill()
  }
}

# Finalize the plot
p + theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Coefficient Heatmap per Neighborhood (Each Variable Has Own Fill Scale)",
    x = "Variable", y = "Neighborhood"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(MASS)  # For polr()
library(tidyr)

# Run models per neighborhood
models_per_ward <- merged_data %>%
  group_split(sec_neigh) %>%
  setNames(unique(merged_data$sec_neigh)) %>%
  lapply(function(df) {
    neigh <- unique(df$sec_neigh)[1]  # Get first unique neighborhood name
    print(paste("Processing", neigh, "Rows:", nrow(df)))
    
    # Skip small groups
    if (nrow(df) < 5) return(NULL)

    # Convert categorical response
    df$class_max <- as.ordered(df$class_max)

    # Remove NAs again
    df <- df %>% drop_na(tract_white_perc, Bedrooms, Land.Square.Feet, 
                         Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land., Age)

    # Check if df is empty after removing NAs
    if (nrow(df) == 0) {
      print(paste("Skipping", neigh, "- no valid rows after drop_na()"))
      return(NULL)
    }

    # Try fitting model safely
    tryCatch({
      polr(class_max ~ tract_white_perc + Bedrooms + Land.Square.Feet + 
                   Prior.Tax.Year.Market.Value.Estimate..Land. + Age, 
           data = df, method = "logistic")
    }, error = function(e) {
      print(paste("Error in", neigh))
      print(e)
      return(NULL)
    })
    
    
  })


library(ggplot2)
library(broom)  # For tidy()
# Ensure that models_per_ward contains only successfully fitted models
valid_models <- models_per_ward[!sapply(models_per_ward, is.null)]

# Extract coefficients into a data frame
coef_list <- lapply(names(valid_models), function(neigh) {
  model <- valid_models[[neigh]]
  if (is.null(model)) return(NULL)  # Skip failed models
  
  tryCatch({
    coefs <- tidy(model)  # Extract coefficients safely
    coefs$Neighborhood <- neigh  # Add neighborhood name
    return(coefs)
  }, error = function(e) {
    print(paste("Error extracting coefficients for", neigh))
    print(e)
    return(NULL)
  })
})

# Combine into one dataframe
coef_df <- bind_rows(coef_list)

# Check if coef_df is empty before visualization
if (nrow(coef_df) > 0) {
  # Heatmap of coefficients
  ggplot(coef_df, aes(x = term, y = Neighborhood, fill = estimate)) +
    geom_tile() +
    scale_fill_gradient2(low = "blue", high = "red", mid = "white", midpoint = 0) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "Coefficient Heatmap per Neighborhood",
         x = "Variable", y = "Neighborhood")

  # Dot plot of coefficients
  ggplot(coef_df, aes(x = estimate, y = term, color = Neighborhood)) +
    geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
    theme_minimal() +
    labs(title = "Coefficient Dot Plot per Neighborhood",
         x = "Coefficient", y = "Variable") +
    theme(legend.position = "none")  # Hide legend if too many neighborhoods
} else {
  print("No valid coefficient data to visualize.")
}
```

```{r}
library(boot)
library(boot)

# Define the bootstrap statistic function
bootstrap_stratified <- function(data, indices) {
  # Use the indices provided by boot() to sample data
  sampled_data <- data[indices, ] %>%
    group_by(ward) %>%
    sample_n(size = min(table(data$ward)), replace = TRUE) %>%  # Balance wards
    ungroup()
  
  # Calculate the 90th percentile for each ward
  percentile_90 <- sampled_data %>%
    group_by(ward) %>%
    summarise(Max_90th = quantile(Max, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(Max_90th)  # Extract the 90th percentile values
  
  return(percentile_90)
}

set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility

# Perform bootstrapping with 200 iterations
boot_results <- boot(data = finalidk, statistic = bootstrap_stratified, R = 200)

# View the results
print(boot_results)

library(boot)

# Perform bootstrapping with 200 iterations
boot_results <- boot(data = finalidk, statistic = bootstrap_stratified, R = 200)

# Compute confidence intervals for the bootstrap estimates
ci_results <- boot.ci(boot_results, type = c("perc"))

# Print the confidence intervals
print(ci_results)

```


```{r}
# Extract the bootstrap replicates (results for each ward)
boot_replicates <- boot_results$t

# Calculate the 95% confidence intervals for each ward (percentile method)
ci_data <- apply(boot_replicates, 2, function(x) {
  quantiles <- quantile(x, probs = c(0.025, 0.975))  # 95% CI
  return(quantiles)
})

# Convert the CI data to a data frame for plotting
ci_df <- data.frame(
  ward = 1:ncol(boot_replicates),  # assuming the number of columns corresponds to wards
  lower = ci_data[1, ],  # lower bound of CI
  upper = ci_data[2, ],  # upper bound of CI
  original = boot_results$t0  # original statistic (e.g., the 90th percentile)
)

# Plot the confidence intervals
ggplot(ci_df, aes(x = ward, y = original)) +
  geom_point(color = "blue") +  # Original statistic as points
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.1, color = "red") +  # Confidence intervals as error bars
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Bootstrap Confidence Intervals for Each Ward",
       x = "Ward", y = "90th Percentile") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# Make sure draw columns are numeric
finalidk$Draw1 <- as.numeric(finalidk$Draw1)
finalidk$Draw2 <- as.numeric(finalidk$Draw2)
finalidk$Draw3 <- as.numeric(finalidk$Draw3)

# Step 1: Reshape and prep data without pivoting full data
draw_stats_by_group <- finalidk %>%
  group_by(MaxSource) %>%
  summarise(
    Median_Draw1 = median(Draw1, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Draw2 = median(Draw2, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median_Draw3 = median(Draw3, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD1 = sd(Draw1, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD2 = sd(Draw2, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD3 = sd(Draw3, na.rm = TRUE),
    N1 = sum(!is.na(Draw1)),
    N2 = sum(!is.na(Draw2)),
    N3 = sum(!is.na(Draw3)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    SE1 = SD1 / sqrt(N1),
    SE2 = SD2 / sqrt(N2),
    SE3 = SD3 / sqrt(N3)
  ) %>%
  # Reshape for plotting
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("Median_Draw"),
    names_to = "Draw",
    values_to = "Median"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Draw_Num = as.numeric(gsub("Median_Draw", "", Draw)),
    SE = case_when(
      Draw_Num == 1 ~ SD1 / sqrt(N1),
      Draw_Num == 2 ~ SD2 / sqrt(N2),
      Draw_Num == 3 ~ SD3 / sqrt(N3)
    )
  )

# Step 2: Plot
ggplot(draw_stats_by_group, aes(x = Draw_Num, y = Median)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "steelblue", size = 2) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Median - SE, ymax = Median + SE),
                width = 0.2, color = "gray40") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:3, labels = c("Draw1", "Draw2", "Draw3")) +
  labs(
    title = "Median Lead Level by Draw, Faceted by MaxSource",
    x = "Draw Number",
    y = "Median Lead Level (µg/L)"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ MaxSource) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)
```

```{r}
# Function to compute bootstrap SE for a ward
bootstrap_se <- function(data, n_boot = 1000) {
  boot_vals <- replicate(n_boot, {
    sample_data <- sample(data$Max, replace = TRUE)
    quantile(sample_data, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  return(sd(boot_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
}
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Function to compute 90th percentile and SE using bootstrap
bootstrap_percentile_se_ci <- function(data, n_boot = 1000) {
  boot_vals <- replicate(n_boot, {
    sample_data <- sample(data$Max, replace = TRUE)
    quantile(sample_data, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  
  est <- quantile(data$Max, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
  se <- sd(boot_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
  ci_lower <- est - 1.96 * se
  ci_upper <- est + 1.96 * se
  
  return(tibble(Max_90th = est, SE = se, CI_lower = ci_lower, CI_upper = ci_upper))
}

# Apply to each ward
percentile_ci <- finalidk %>%
  group_by(ward) %>%
  group_modify(~ bootstrap_percentile_se_ci(.x))

```

```{r}
   coord_flip() +

    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    axis.title.x = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.title.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold"),
    axis.text.y = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "right"
  )

```



```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

# Function to compute bootstrap 95% CI for a ward
bootstrap_ci <- function(data, n_boot = 8000) {
  boot_vals <- replicate(n_boot, {
    sample_data <- sample(data$Max, replace = TRUE)
    quantile(sample_data, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE)
  })
  quantile(boot_vals, probs = c(0.025, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
}

# Apply to each ward
percentile_ci <- finalidk %>%
  group_by(ward) %>%
  summarise(
    Max_90th = quantile(Max, 0.90, na.rm = TRUE),
    CI_lower = bootstrap_ci(cur_data())[1],
    CI_upper = bootstrap_ci(cur_data())[2]
  )

```



```{r}

                width = 0.3, color = "black") +
   geom_hline(yintercept = 15, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +  # Red dashed line at 15
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, color = "red", linetype = "dashed", size = 1) +
   annotate("text", x = 1, y = 15, label = "15 ppb", color = "red", vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold") +
```
